input.quote: (i) All paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the General Matters provisions (20(a)–(i)) contain no coverage or certificate requirement, nor do the delivery/installation (§4) or implementation (§9) provisions. Garman installs the Software at our Authorized Locations and converts Sparkling's data (§4(a)–(b)) and provides ongoing maintenance and support, so it is an on-premises vendor with access to our data — the rule expects insurance and the absence falls into walk-away territory. Inserted the playbook's model coverage as new Section 20(j) after the final General Matters subsection, offering the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback in the comment.

proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance provision as new Section 20(j)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance provision even though Garman installs software at our locations and converts our data, so we have added our standard coverage requirements (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Garman handles our data) with certificates on request. If these limits are an issue, we can discuss E&O of USD 1,000,000 and cyber of USD 2,000,000 as a fallback.

ops.text: (j) Garman shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law; and, where Garman processes, stores or has access to Sparkling's data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Garman shall provide certificates of insurance to Sparkling on request.
